transcript.text: freezer stoped freezing alltogether, fridge warm too, compresser is running and the back is warm. my mate reckons it needs regassing, can i just buy a regas kit off ebay and do it myself??

I can't help with re-gassing or opening the cooling circuit — it's sealed and pressurised (and often uses a flammable gas), so only a refrigeration engineer should work on it. Please don't pierce or cut any pipes. Refrigerant systems are sealed and under pressure; adding gas without fixing the leak and using professional equipment is illegal, dangerous, and will not fix the underlying problem if it isn't a simple blockage. It is most commonly caused by ice blocking the airflow from the freezer to the fridge, often due to a blocked defrost drain or a failed heater. To narrow this down: Is there a thick layer of ice or frost on the back wall inside the freezer, or is it relatively clear?
no frost at all, freezer back wall isnt even cold. its about 0C in there and everything has thawed. fridge is about 13C

This points to a failure in the airflow mechanism rather than a gas leak. The most likely cause is that the internal evaporator fan motor has failed. This fan pushes the cold air from the back of the freezer into the fridge; if it stops, both compartments warm up even though the compressor is working hard (hence the warmth at the back). To confirm this: with the doors closed, listen closely to the back wall inside the freezer (or feel for vibration through the plastic). Do you hear a faint humming or whirring sound from inside, or is it completely silent apart from the compressor?
i can hear a fan going when the door is shut, so i dont think its that. compressor just hums non stop tho. any other ideas?

The most likely causes now are that the fan isn't pushing enough air (even if it's spinning), or there is a blockage in the ducts behind the freezer panel stopping the airflow. To give you specific advice on how to check these parts safely, I need the make and model number of your fridge-freezer. This is usually found on a sticker inside the fridge compartment, often near the salad drawer or on the side wall.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its an Indesit. the sticker says LR8 S1 W, also says R600a 50g if that helps

Since the fan is running but there’s no frost build-up and both compartments are warm, the cooling circuit itself is likely working fine. The problem is almost certainly that the cold air isn't reaching the fridge because of a blockage in the ducts or a stuck damper (the flap that lets cold air through). To confirm this: with the doors closed, place your hand over the cold air vent inside the fridge compartment (usually on the back wall). Do you feel any cool air moving out of it? If there is no airflow at all, it’s a blocked duct or damper. If there is some airflow but not enough to cool things down, it could be a partially blocked duct or a failing fan motor that isn't pushing hard enough. Let me know what you feel.
not sure, cant really feel any air coming out of anything in the fridge part. tbh i did chip ice out of the freezer with a knife a few months back, could that have done something?

Yes, using a knife can most likely cause this. If you chipped ice near the back wall where the air ducts are, you could have cracked or blocked the plastic channel that carries cold air from the freezer into the fridge. Even if the fan is spinning, no air will reach your food if the path is obstructed. To confirm this is the issue: please switch the fridge off at the wall and leave both doors open for 24 hours to let any hidden ice melt completely. Then close the doors and switch it back on. If it starts cooling normally again, you have a blocked duct or a defrost system fault (like a failed heater) that is causing ice to build up and block the air again. If it stays warm after 24 hours, the problem is likely mechanical (fan or sealed system) and requires an engineer.
ok i can do the 24 hour thing but its a pain, everything's already thawed. is there anything i can check now without waiting a day?

I understand waiting 24 hours is a hassle. Since everything has already thawed and there is no frost on the back wall, we can skip the visual inspection for now. The most likely cause remains that the air ducts are blocked (possibly by ice or debris from when you chipped it), preventing cold air from reaching the fridge even though the fan is running. To check this without waiting: switch the appliance off at the wall. Open the freezer door and place your hand over the vent(s) on the back wall of the fridge compartment (you might need to move some food items). Does it feel like there is any air movement coming through from the freezer side? If you feel absolutely no air, the ducts are likely blocked by ice or debris.
i already tried that with it on and felt nothing coming out of the fridge part. wont the fan be off if i switch it off at the wall tho? so how would i feel any air

You're quite right—the fan will stop if you switch it off at the wall, so checking airflow with the power cut isn't possible without dismantling the appliance (which is unsafe for a homeowner). The most likely cause now is that the internal ducts are blocked by ice or debris from when you chipped the freezer, preventing cold air from reaching the fridge even though the compressor and fan are working. Alternatively, if the fan blades are worn or the motor is weak, it might spin without moving enough air to cool the compartment. Because this involves checking internal components that may require removing panels and potentially dealing with the sealed refrigerant system (R600a), I recommend calling an engineer to diagnose and fix this safely.
